name: Question 16
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063571/assets/b6d469b24061f0f7284691b2e2f26a2c28d9557ab72a1c8ba3cad93eb65dde91.png)

Evaluate the triple integral 
${∭}_{R}2{z}^{2}\,dV$
over the region $R,$ shown above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the right one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063571/assets/9190139502ef900218e3c3b186295627af2a1370b9f7d789366dac6474251b54.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type III region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le y=3-\frac{x}{3}-z},
$$

where

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,0\le z\le 2}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063571/assets/aa02840c9fa15e5e5048608fff81ad9f0a5623821a57366bf12ec6d60332bc9e.png)

Hence, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 3-\frac{x}{3}-z}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}2{z}^{2}\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3-x/3-z}2{z}^{2}\,dy\,dz\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3-x/3-z}2{z}^{2}\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{3-x/3-z}2{z}^{2}\,dy]dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}2{z}^{2}[y]_{y=0}^{y=3-x/3-z}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}2{z}^{2}(3-\frac{x}{3}-z)\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}(6{z}^{2}-\frac{2}{3}x{z}^{2}-2{z}^{3})\,dz\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}(6{z}^{2}-\frac{2}{3}x{z}^{2}-2{z}^{3})\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{0}^{2}(6{z}^{2}-\frac{2}{3}x{z}^{2}-2{z}^{3})\,dz]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{[2{z}^{3}-\frac{2}{9}x{z}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{z}^{4}]}_{z=0}^{z=2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(8-\frac{16}{9}x)\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}(8-\frac{16}{9}x)\,dx & ={[8x-\frac{16}{18}{x}^{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=3} \\  & =(24-8)-0 \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Notice that our solid can be written as the type III region

R={(x,y,z):(x,z)∈D,0≤y≤y=3−x3−z},

where

D={(x,z):0≤x≤3,0≤z≤2}

is the projection of R onto the xz-plane, shown below.

Hence, the type III representation of R is

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤3,0≤z≤2,0≤y≤3−x3−z}

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

∭R2z2dV=∫03∫02∫03−x/3−z2z2dydzdx.

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to y, treating x and z as constants:

∫03∫02∫03−x/3−z2z2dydzdx=∫03∫02[∫03−x/3−z2z2dy]dzdx=∫03∫022z2[y]y=0y=3−x/3−zdzdx=∫03∫022z2(3−x3−z)dzdx=∫03∫02(6z2−23xz2−2z3)dzdx

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to z, treating x as a constant:

∫03∫02(6z2−23xz2−2z3)dzdx=∫03[∫02(6z2−23xz2−2z3)dz]dx=∫03[2z3−29xz3−12z4]z=0z=2dx=∫03(8−169x)dx

Finally, we integrate with respect to x:

∫03(8−169x)dx=[8x−1618x2]x=0x=3=(24−8)−0=16.
